method_note: Values were read from: the Nature HTML of 2026Natur.657..359A with its Extended Data Table 2 image (Tab2_ESM.jpg), cross-checked against arXiv:2607.12664v1; arXiv PDFs of the other papers (pdftotext -layout, and pypdf for Greek column headers and for tables whose layout text scrambled rows); the Nature table image for Ciurlo 2020 Extended Data Table 3; SIMBAD TAP (identifiers, otype, sp_type/sp_bibcode, K flux and bibcode; ref table for bibcode/DOI/title); Crossref for two DOIs. ADS was not used (captcha). Nothing was computed, converted or estimated: a stays in the unit printed (mas, arcsec, mpc or AU), P/tP/rp only where printed, and anything not printed is null. Dusty/gas G-objects are included in new_stars with an object_class label because the brief asked for their orbits; they are not confirmed stars. Asymmetric errors are stored as err_plus/err_minus with err null.

s301.status: confirmed by its discoverers only (GRAVITY+ Collaboration); no independent detection by another group yet. Published in Nature after peer review.

orbit.solution: 1 of 2 (left column of Extended Data Table 2; the one whose posterior is Extended Data Fig. 5)
orbit.a_note: Table gives a in mas; a_arcsec left null rather than converted.
orbit.where: Extended Data Table 2 'Best-fit orbit parameters for S301' (image Tab2_ESM.jpg on the Nature article page, read directly; identical numbers in arXiv:2607.12664v1 p. 20). Caption: 'The two sets give the two possible orbit orientations.'
orbit.mass_r0_note: Main text, 'Observations and data analysis': 'The potential is defined by the central mass fixed with M_MBH = 4.297 x 10^6 Msun at a distance of R0 = 8,277 pc. We do not allow for any coordinate system offsets, as our data are interferometrically referenced directly to the near-infrared counterpart of Sgr A*.' M and R0 were fixed, not fitted.
orbit.conventions: Row order a, e, i, Omega, omega, tP, then P and chi2 (Greek glyphs read from the table image). Methods 'Best-fit orbit': '(angle conventions follow ref. 4)' = Gillessen et al. 2009, ApJ 692, 1075 (2009ApJ...692.1075G), i.e. the MPE/GRAVITY convention in which the ascending node is the receding one (docs/architecture/galactic-centre.md); ref. 4 itself defines Omega as the 'angle of the line of nodes' and omega as the 'angle from ascending node to pericenter'. The fit is relativistic: 'taking into account Romer delay and the 1PN correction ... Schwarzschild' (Methods), as for S2 in GRAVITY 2020 (A&A 636 L5), so the elements are osculating; the paper does not state an osculation epoch. No radial velocity exists, so the node is ambiguous: the two solutions differ by ~183 deg in Omega and ~178 deg in omega, i.e. they are (almost) the mirror pair through the sky plane. The repo's sky_elements 180-deg turn therefore cannot pick between them.
orbit.fit_stats: chi2 = 26 for 34 degrees of freedom (main text); 19 astrometric positions 2017 (weak inference), 2021, 2023-2025 (Methods, Extended Data Table 1).

orbit_alt.solution: 2 of 2 (right column of Extended Data Table 2)
orbit_alt.note: The main text gives this solution's eccentricity as 0.9821 ('e = 0.9832 and 0.9821 (for the two possible orientations)'); the table prints 0.9824. Both the Nature HTML table and arXiv v1 table say 0.9824; table value used. Methods notes 'the orbital plane of one of the two possible solutions agrees to within 3 deg with the inner clockwise disk of young, massive stars in ref. 32' (von Fellenberg 2022) without saying which.

rp_RS.where: Main text: 'pericentre distance rp of only 136 RS and 142 RS, respectively' (solution 1, 2).

v_peri_kms.where: Main text: 'about 25,600 km/s or 8.5% of c and 25,000 km/s or 8.3% of c, respectively'.

precession_deg_per_orbit.where: Main text: 'relativistic pericentre advance per orbit amounts to 2.0 deg and 1.9 deg'.

derived_in_text.discovery: Spring 2023, '15 mas northwest of Sgr A*' (main text).

kmag.where: Abstract ('mK = 19.3') and 'Observations and data analysis': 'we derive a K-band magnitude of mK = 19.3 +/- 0.3', calibrated on brighter sources with photometry from ref. 4.

spectral_type.where: Methods 'Spectral type, mass and age of S301': with A_K = 2.42 and R0 = 8.3 kpc, M_K ~ 2.28; 'a late A-type or an early F-type star ... V-K = 0.6 ... absolute V magnitude of 2.88, it has L = 5.5 Lsun and a spectral type of F1.5'. Inferred from photometry only: 'we have not been able to detect it as a continuum source or from spectral features' in ERIS spectroscopy.

mass_msun.where: Main text: 'a mass <~1.5 Msun'; Methods: 'a mass of just below 1.5 Msun. Alternatively ... between approximately 1.1 Msun and 1.5 Msun, depending on the age' (MIST and PARSEC tracks, Extended Data Fig. 8). No single value with an error is given; the collision estimate uses 'm* ~ 1.5 Msun and R* ~ 1.4 Rsun'.

rv_kms.where: 'we do not yet have any radial velocity information' (main text); this is the cause of the two-fold orbit ambiguity.

s301.other_new_stars_in_paper: None with elements. Fig. 1 labels Sgr A*, S21, S24, S29, S38, S42, S55, S62 (GRAVITY's), S63, S301 and 'SX' ('a potential source not yet rediscovered' in the 2021 image). No S300/S302 elements are given.
s301.follow_ups: Later papers reuse Extended Data Table 2 rather than refit it: arXiv:2609.06936 (Catanzarite, Table 1 'Adopted S301 parameters': 8.68 yr, e = 0.9832, 136 RS), arXiv:2607.24931 (Piran et al., quotes e = 0.9825, rp = 280 rg), arXiv:2609.07693 (GRAVITY+ Yukawa fit including S301 data 2023.25-2025.36; no new S301 element table found). None is an independent measurement.

caveats: S301 has two equally good orbits (no RV): Omega 73.8 / 256.9 and omega 293.4 / 115.1 are almost exactly the sky-plane mirror pair. The repo's sky_elements turns Omega and omega by 180 deg, which here maps one solution approximately onto the other -- so for S301 the drawn orbit's z-sign is not physically determined either way. Solution 1 is listed as 'orbit' only because it is the left column and the one plotted in Extended Data Fig. 5.
S301 eccentricity of the second solution: text 0.9821, table 0.9824 (both Nature and arXiv v1). Table used.

S301 elements come from a 1PN (Schwarzschild + Romer) fit with M and R0 fixed at the L12 values; they are osculating, and the osculation epoch is not stated. Pure Kepler propagation will drift (~2 deg of pericentre advance per 8.7-yr orbit).
S301 mass, spectral type and luminosity are inferred from mK = 19.3 alone (no spectrum): F1.5, ~5.5 Lsun, 1.1-1.5 Msun depending on age. No single mass value is printed, so mass_msun.value is null.

von Fellenberg 2022 Table 4: several rows print sigma_e equal to sigma_a (R14 0.08, R30 0.14, R39 1.46, R44 0.48, R85 1.7, S97 0.38, S72 0.05, R1 0.06) -- probably a column-copy error in the paper; recorded as printed. Small errors are printed as '>0.01' (presumably '<0.01') in some rows of stars already on the tab; the eight new stars all have numeric errors.

von Fellenberg 2022 pypdf text runs adjacent cells together (e.g. '158.8 1.171659.39'); every value was split by the two-decimal pattern and cross-checked against Kepler's third law only as a sanity check (not used to change any value).

von Fellenberg 2022 says '31 were presented in previous studies (Gillessen et al. 2009, 2017) ... Five stars have newly found orbital solutions' but does not say which five. By name, eight of its 36 are absent from Gillessen 2017 (R1, R14, R30, R39, R70, R85, S5, S72) and S5 is in Gillessen 2009, leaving seven -- the paper's counts do not reconcile with this, possibly via orbits in other MPE papers. All eight are recorded.

SIMBAD disagrees with von Fellenberg 2022 on two identifications: S72 (vF: = E18 = S1-8; SIMBAD: E18 = S1-8 = W11, a separate object from [EG97] S72) and R70 (vF: = E54 = S4-36; SIMBAD: E54 = IRS 34E, a separate object from [GKM98] S4-36). K mags/spectral types for those two are therefore conditional.

Ali et al. 2020 (Cologne) is the only source for S64. The same table gives S29 a 34.7 mpc, e 0.335, tclos 2054.6, which GRAVITY's interferometric S29 orbit (pericentre 2021.41, e ~0.97; L12, A82) contradicts. Ali's inclinations also cluster near 90 deg and the paper flags RV-less inclination ambiguities. Treat S64 as low confidence.

Dusty objects (G1, G2, G3_Gillessen2025, D2/G3_Ciurlo, G4, G5, G6/X8, X7, X7.1, D3, D3.1, D5, D23, D9, OS1, OS2) are in new_stars only because the brief asked for their orbits; each carries object_class. None is a confirmed star except possibly D9 (claimed Herbig Ae/Be + T Tauri binary by one group). D3.1 is a filament per its own authors.
Two different objects are called G3: Ciurlo 2020's G3 (= D2, a dusty source) and Gillessen 2025's G3 (a gas clump on the G1/G2 orbit). They are separate entries.

Where two groups published orbits for the same dusty object, they often disagree beyond their errors (D2/G3: Omega 221 vs 55 deg; X8/G6: e 0.99 vs 0.41; X7: a 150 mpc vs 4800 AU). Peissker's and Ciurlo's papers do not state whether the ascending node is the receding one, so some Omega/omega differences may be convention, but X7 and X8/G6 differ in a and e too.

Peissker group papers use M = 4.0e6 Msun / R0 = 8 kpc (D9, ERIS 2025) or do not state M/R0 (2024 A&A Table 5); Ciurlo 2020 uses 3.964e6 / 7.971 kpc; Ciurlo 2023 4.07e6 / 8.1 kpc; Ali 2020 4.3e6 / 8.3 kpc; Witzel 2017 3.93e6 / 7.87 kpc; MPE 4.296-4.297e6 / 8.275-8.277 kpc. None was converted.

Bibcodes 2024A&A...686A.235P and 2024NatCo..1510608P were built from Crossref journal/volume/article numbers and are not confirmed in SIMBAD or ADS (ADS abstract pages show a captcha). 2025A&A...704A...7P and 2026A&A...707A..79G are from SIMBAD's ref table. All other bibcodes were confirmed against SIMBAD's ref table.

Not accessed: ADS (captcha); the published typeset versions of the arXiv papers (arXiv versions used, except the S301 Nature HTML and Ciurlo 2020 Nature table image); Gillessen 2009's S5/S27 elements (pre-window, not extracted); Meyer 2012 supplement (S0-104).

No other new star with a published full orbit was found in GRAVITY/GRAVITY+ papers 2021-2026: A127 (S62 GRAVITY, linear), A82 (S300 linear; Table 5 updates S2, S29, S38, S42, S55, S60 only), L12 and A242 (four stars), the S301 Nature paper, and the 2026 Yukawa paper (S2, S29, S38, S55, S301).
